args.goal: Check full mission history for an equivalent funded-bounty assessment, including prior GitHub discovery refusals, and reuse any current evidence. Test one public bounty board offering maintainer-funded software work, such as Algora. Use at most three public GETs, including the board and the original issue or bounty terms. Use no renewed requests for a source the host rejected. Select at most one live, explicitly funded documentation, example-validation or non-personal data-quality task whose acceptance criterion can be checked offline. Exclude security, exploit, intrusion and authenticated customer-system work. Before drafting a submission, execute the smallest useful acceptance check and preserve the actual output, original requirement quotation and source hash. Save a reviewable patch or worked sample if the repository license and source support it. Verify contributor and disclosed AI eligibility, invited submission route, competing-claim rules and payout compatibility separately. Provide a copy-ready operator handoff only when those terms support it. If no task qualifies, preserve the precise coverage and a concrete reopening condition without inferring market-wide demand. Read back committed evidence and close under a valid lease with a lesson. No account creation, external submission, spending or deployment. Preserve host-enforced independent review of any public release.
